title: Erdős Problem #260: Irrationality of Sparse Sequence Series
description: If a₁ < a₂ < ⋯ is increasing with aₙ/n → ∞, is ∑ aₙ/2^{aₙ} necessarily irrational?

meta.author: Erdős (1974)
originalContributions: Defined the series ∑ aₙ/2^{aₙ} with partial sums and convergence
Developed the n² sequence as a concrete example
Stated the main conjecture: fast growth alone implies irrationality
Proved convergence of the series under fast growth
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: erdos_260_conjecture (open conjecture). 3 sorries: series_converges (convergence argument), irrational_of_gaps_to_infinity (Erdős 1974 theorem), irrational_of_superlogarithmic (number-theoretic result).

overview.historicalContext:
This problem originates from Erdős's 1974 work on irrationality of series [Er74b], further developed in the landmark monograph 'Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory' with Graham [ErGr80]. It explores a fundamental question at the boundary of analysis and number theory: when does a lacunary (sparse) series produce an irrational sum?

Erdős proved that irrationality holds under the stronger condition that the gaps a_{n+1} − aₙ tend to infinity. He also showed irrationality when aₙ grows superlogarithmically, specifically when aₙ ≫ n√(log n · log log n). These partial results demonstrate that 'sufficiently fast' growth guarantees irrationality, but the full conjecture — that the mere condition aₙ/n → ∞ suffices — remains open.

The problem has an appealing simplicity: the series ∑ aₙ/2^{aₙ} converges absolutely for any increasing sequence (the terms decrease exponentially), so the question is purely about the arithmetic nature of the limit. Erdős and Graham speculated that even having limsup of the gaps being infinite might not suffice for irrationality, but no counterexample has been found. The problem connects to the theory of lacunary series, normal numbers, and the Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem.
overview.problemStatement: Let $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be an increasing sequence of natural numbers with $a_n/n \to \infty$. Is the sum $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n / 2^{a_n}$ necessarily irrational?
overview.text: If a₁ < a₂ < ⋯ is increasing with aₙ/n → ∞, is ∑ aₙ/2^{aₙ} necessarily irrational?
overview.proofStrategy: We formalize several growth conditions on sequences: IncreasingSeq (strictly increasing), FastGrowth (aₙ/n → ∞), GapsToInfinity (gaps → ∞), and SuperlogarithmicGrowth. The series and its convergence are defined. Erdős's known partial results (irrationality under gaps-to-infinity and superlogarithmic growth) are stated as theorems with sorry. The sequence aₙ = n² is developed as a concrete example. The main conjecture is stated as an axiom.
keyInsights: **Gaps-to-Infinity Theorem**: Erdős proved that if a_{n+1} − aₙ → ∞, the series is irrational. This uses approximation by rational numbers and gap separation
**Superlogarithmic Threshold**: Irrationality also holds for aₙ ≫ n√(log n · log log n), providing a quantitative growth threshold
**Square Sequence Example**: The sequence aₙ = n² has gaps 2n+1 → ∞, so its series ∑ n²/2^{n²} is irrational by the gaps theorem
**Counterexample Gap**: Erdős-Graham speculated that limsup(gaps) = ∞ alone may not suffice, but no counterexample exists — the problem's difficulty lies in this gap
**Lacunary Series**: The problem belongs to the rich theory of lacunary series, where sparsity of terms interacts with arithmetic properties of sums

sections.title: Header and Imports
sections.summary: States Erdős Problem #260 on irrationality of $\sum 1/a_n$ for fast-growing increasing integer sequences. Defines the `IncreasingSeq` structure and sets up imports. The conjecture: fast growth forces irrationality.
sections.mathContext: Erdős #260: does fast growth of $(a_n)$ force $\sum 1/a_n$ irrational? `IncreasingSeq` structure.

sections.title: Part II: The Series
sections.summary: Defines `seriesTerm`, `partialSum`, `seriesSum` ($\sum 1/a_n$), and states `series_converges` (the series converges — proof `sorry`).

sections.title: Part III: Known Irrationality Results

sections.title: Part VI: The Main Conjecture

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: Closing comments recapping the conjecture, the proved square-sequence example, the growth-condition implications, and the remaining sorries (convergence and the two irrationality results).
sections.mathContext: Recap: conjecture (axiom), $n^2$ example proved; 3 sorries (convergence + 2 irrationality results).

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #260 asks whether the series ∑ aₙ/2^{aₙ} is irrational whenever aₙ/n → ∞. Erdős proved irrationality under the stronger conditions of gaps tending to infinity or superlogarithmic growth. The gap between these partial results and the full conjecture remains the central open question.
conclusion.implications: A proof would establish that growth rate alone determines the arithmetic nature of these lacunary series. A counterexample would reveal subtle structure in rational-summing sparse sequences and would likely require innovative constructions in combinatorial number theory.
openQuestions: Can the gaps-to-infinity condition be weakened to mere fast growth while preserving irrationality?
Does there exist a sequence with unbounded but non-tending-to-infinity gaps that gives a rational sum?
What is the minimal growth rate guaranteeing irrationality?
Does the base 2 play a special role, or does the result hold for other bases?
Can methods from the theory of continued fractions or Padé approximants make progress?
